findings.review_scope: Registered-source review of Change point inference in high-dimensional regression models under temporal dependence by Haotian Xu, Daren Wang, Zifeng Zhao and Yi Yu. The verified 112-page file is arXiv:2207.12453v3; its margin date is 1 October 2023 and title-page date 3 October 2023. Main text and references occupy pages 1-33. Only the Appendices heading was inspected on page 34, using a crop ending at y=89. Appendix bodies were excluded.
findings.inventory: Four actual bold Theorem environments: Theorem 3 on pages 12-13, Theorem 4 on page 17, Theorem 8 on page 18 and Theorem 10 on page 21. All complete statements were compared with rendered PDF pages. Four ordinary-font mentions and Lemmas, Propositions and Remarks are excluded from the theorem inventory. A fresh font-aware scan covers all 33 permitted pages and separately verifies Assumptions 1-4.
original_statements: Theorem 3 retains Assumptions 1,2,3,4b; all four setup bullets; DPDU tuning with the square-root logarithm and 2/gamma-1 exponent; the two regimes and both estimation rates. Its integer random walk retains the negative-side minus sign, positive-side plus sign, exact summation endpoints and extra paired-process convergence assumption. Its real Brownian limit retains varpi/sigma, both independent Brownian halves and the normalized jump reference.

Theorem 4 concerns a mean-zero potentially nonstationary scalar process, with a time-uniform second-moment functional dependence measure, exponential-power decay, uniform tails and gamma(Z)<1. Both deviation terms, x>=1 and integer m>=3 are preserved. Its tail-exponent coefficient is one, distinct from the regression combined exponent.

Theorem 8 retains all inherited assumptions and notation, each algorithm input, the estimated coefficient indices as printed and the integer block-count condition length>>R>>sqrt(length). The maximum runs through true K. The printed convergence-in-probability label P. retains its period.

Theorem 10 retains M=infinity, the squared jump estimate wording, the population/estimated squared-jump ratio, the nonzero-jump indicator and the Brownian limit with sigma multiplying W. Equation (30) defines the unsquared estimate; that difference is documented rather than repaired.
source_passages: All 33 local source passages and 13 auxiliary excerpts were compared with the rendered main text. The regression model and endpoints on pages 1-2, single-bar vector versus double-bar random-variable norms and stochastic orders on page 4, and causal process/coupling constructions on pages 5-6 remain literal.

Stationary covariate and stationary noise definitions use distinct innovation symbols. Generic innovation replacement is ambient context shared by those processes and the nonstationary scalar construction; it does not import covariate-model assumptions into Theorem 4. Covariate dependence is uniform over all unit directions; nonstationary dependence is uniform over time.

Assumptions 1-4b retain conditional mean-zero noise without independence, time-varying sparse supports, fixed positive K, the coefficient jump immediately before eta_k, spacing and bounded jumps, marginal covariance, positive limiting drift, projection-uniform tails, fourth-moment dependence and baseline-plus-strengthened signal-spacing conditions. The shared exponents are minima of covariate/noise exponents and the regression exponent retains factor two.

The interval Lasso, interval loss and partition objective on pages 6-7 preserve square-root-length penalty scaling, the omitted response-square sum, short-interval zero loss and the single common zeta. Algorithm 1 on page 8 retains its complete initialization, backward moment updates, conditional fit and pointer updates, backtracking start and outputs.

The local interval, final split estimator and preliminary coefficient notation on page 9 retain their exact weights and indices. Lemma 2 on page 12 provides the variance definition and a separate complete existence assertion. The jump estimator (30), variance Algorithm 2, drift estimator (31) and simulated minimizer (32) match pages 18-20.

Algorithm 2 retains k and k+1 coefficient indices, paired-block differences and the estimated-jump normalization. Simulation retains ceiling on the negative side, floor on the positive side, the finite Gaussian index range, positive finite M in Step 1 and the theorem specialization M=infinity. No Brownian interpolation is substituted.
findings.dependency_review: All 62 direct uses, 87 related connections and 33 local dependency lists were checked. Theorem 4 reaches only the nonstationary scalar process and its dependence measure, not the regression assumptions. Theorems 8 and 10 inherit the required regression conditions, tuning and algorithmic constructions in the vanishing-regime context stated in Section 4. Their statements do not use the final refined-location estimator D27, so it remains related only to Theorem 3. Theorem 10 additionally reaches the drift estimator through its simulated minimizer. Inherited assumptions are distinguished from inherited conclusions. Proof uses of Theorem 4 and appendix-only restricted-eigenvalue results do not create statement edges.
findings.names_and_highlights: All names use natural-language terms from their own source passages or saved naming context. Source model passages, assumptions and definitions retain distinct kinds and labels. Every interface has selectors corresponding to its own source passage or label, with any additional selector occurring in a related theorem. Every related theorem has an explanation identifying its actual symbols or assumption references and any intervening local definitions. Repeated terminology does not merge the three distinct functional-dependence constructions.
findings.source_limitations: All 33 existing source notes were retained. These explicitly address the two source dates; joint stationarity and triangular-array conventions; unspecified process-limit topology; jump indices; fixed K; different dependence moments and exponent formulas; tuning restrictions; DPDU pointer bounds, row/column orientation, boundary inclusion and output storage; coefficient-index discrepancies; noninteger local endpoints; argmin selection; variance finiteness versus positivity; vanishing-regime scope; block-count versus block-width and unequal floor identities; division by a zero estimated jump; finite-sample drift versus its limit; squared-estimator wording; finite versus infinite simulation range; step-function paths and unspecified Gaussian/data joint construction. These notes describe source ambiguities and do not certify proofs or repair algorithms.
findings.changes: No census-content correction was required. All six content JSON artifacts and the historical paper audit remain unchanged. Earlier scripts were archived. The saved rebuild now resolves the registered fixed PDF and regenerates the six artifacts in an empty directory without old temporary-file dependencies. Rebuilding saved extraction does not perform a new semantic review.
findings.validation: Independent inventory and census validation pass. All six regenerated artifacts match saved bytes. Source hash, version, both dates, authors, page count, fresh text on all permitted pages, actual theorem and assumption headings, continuation evidence, all direct and local dependency lists, related paths, source kinds, keywords, selectors and historical artifact hashes were checked in addition to the manual rendered-page review.
